title: Keys lobster mini-season: no diving or snorkeling in manmade water bodies, marinas, or within 300 ft of improved shoreline
effect: From three days before the lobster mini-season, through the mini-season, and for the first five days of the commercial lobster season, diving or snorkeling is unlawful in any manmade water body or marina or within 300 ft of improved residential or commercial shoreline, in incorporated and unincorporated Monroe County unless a city ordinance conflicts.
excerpt: (a) It is a public nuisance and is unlawful for any person to dive or snorkel in any manmade water body or marina, or within 300 feet of an improved residential or commercial shoreline beginning three days prior to the opening of and during the entirety of the lobster mini-season and for the first five days of commercial lobster season.
full: (b) Nothing in this article shall prohibit diving incidental to vessel or dock maintenance, provided the diver performing the maintenance lawfully displays a diver down flag and otherwise complies with the requirements of F.S. ch. 327, or diving and snorkeling in front of his or her property to the center line of the canal or 100 feet of open water. § 26-96: 'This article shall be effective in both incorporated and unincorporated Monroe County to the extent that no conflict exist with a municipal ordinance as provided in Art. VIII § 1(f) of the Florida Constitution.' § 26-99: noncriminal infraction, $50 civil penalty, up to $500 in county court. History § 26-98: (Code 1979, § 5.5-140; Ord. No. 044-2003, § 1; Ord. No. 038-2010, § 2; Ord. No. 001-2013, § 2).
scope: All Monroe County (cities included absent a conflicting city ordinance): manmade water bodies, marinas, and water within 300 ft of improved residential or commercial shoreline. Seasonal window only.
note: Read 7 Oct 2026 through api.municode.com in Chrome (Supplement 33 Update 3, published 15 Jul 2026). Replaces the flyer-based lead. Corrections: trigger is the commercial lobster season, not 'regular season' (same 6 Aug opening); 'manmade water body' is wider than 'canal'. No bridge diving ban is codified (searched spear*, bridge AND diving/snorkel/swim, '300 feet' AND bridge, jump* AND bridge*). Not a spearfishing rule by name, but it bars any in-water spearfisher in those places during the window. 'Improved shoreline' has no dataset: text flag, not a polygon.

cite: Palm Beach County Code, App. G, ch. 13, art. II, div. 1, §§ 13-31 to 13-39 (Laws of Fla. ch. 59-1702)
title: Palm Beach County: no underwater spearfishing at night or within any inlet
effect: In all Palm Beach County salt waters, underwater spearfishing is banned from one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise, banned at all times within any inlet, banned within 150 ft of an anchored boat with people fishing, and needs a diver-down flag in the Intracoastal waters, within 200 yd of inlet jetties, and more than 150 yd offshore.
excerpt: Sec. 13-32. No person shall engage in underwater spear fishing in any of the salt waters of Palm Beach County, Florida, during the period of time from one (1) hour after sunset to one (1) hour before sunrise. Sec. 13-33. No person shall at any time engage in underwater spear fishing within any inlet in Palm Beach County, Florida.
full: § 13-35: 'No person shall engage in underwater spear fishing in the salt waters of Palm Beach County, Florida, within one hundred fifty (150) feet of any anchored boat containing a person or persons engaged in fishing provided that this section shall not apply to those persons who were engaged in underwater spear fishing in the salt waters described in this section immediately prior to and at the time that such boat was anchored.' Session law ch. 59-1702 (HB 1996, filed 18 Jun 1959) s. 1(b) defines underwater spear fishing as spearing 'while the person manipulating such instrument or implement is either under water or floating in the water or swimming', so it reaches freedivers as well as scuba. s. 1(d) 'Intercoastal Waters' are all county territorial waters except those in the Atlantic Ocean. s. 7: flag required within 200 yd of any inlet jetty, not applying inside 150 yd of MHW. s. 8: flag required more than 150 yd from MHW. s. 10 repeals ch. 31133 (1955). County code history notes cite 59-1702 ss. 2 to 9 for §§ 13-32 to 13-39.
scope: All salt waters of Palm Beach County (night ban); every inlet in the county: Jupiter Inlet, Lake Worth Inlet, South Lake Worth (Boynton) Inlet, Boca Raton Inlet (inlet ban). 'Inlet' is undefined.
note: Read 7 Oct 2026: county code through api.municode.com (Supplement 126 Update 1, 7 Jul 2026) and the 1959 session law from the State Library scan (edocs.dlis.state.fl.us/fldocs/leg/actsflorida/1959/LOF1959V2Pt3Ch1670-1754.pdf, printed pp. 3261 to 3263). Wording matches apart from '(1)' numerals and capitalisation. FWC did not repeal 59-1702 in r. 68B-3.038. Applies to freedivers. regs.json already describes these rules but law.json had no entry; the inlet ban is drawn only at Lake Worth Inlet.

title: Hollywood: no spearfishing within 100 yards of the public beach
effect: Spearfishing is prohibited within 100 yards of Hollywood's public/municipal beach, which § 99.01 defines as running from mean high water to 50 yards offshore along the whole Hollywood oceanfront; loaded spearguns are barred on the beach and in public swimming areas.
excerpt: (F) Spearfishing is prohibited within 100 yards of the public/municipal beach. It is unlawful to carry or possess a loaded spear gun on the public/municipal beach or in the public swimming areas. Participants must have fish bag and a raft.
full: Lead-in: 'It shall be unlawful for any person to do any acts set forth below upon Hollywood Beach as described in § 99.01:' (E): 'Swim, bathe or participate in other water activities in the proximity of groins, jetties or other hazards, or, sit, stand, or perform any activity on these structures.' § 99.01 opens: 'All of the area lying east of the mean high water line and north of the common Hollywood-Hallandale city limits and south of an easterly extension of the south right-of-way of Magnolia Terrace and west of a point 50 yards east of said mean high water line;' and continues north to 'south of John U. Lloyd State Park and west of a point 50 yards east of said mean high water line, less that portion in the corporate city limits of Dania, Florida'. § 99.02(B)(4) allows snorkeling or scuba with a diver-down flag. History § 99.03: ('72 Code, § 7½-4) (Ord. O-74-24, passed 3-6-74; ... Am. Ord. O-2023-04, passed 4-4-23).
scope: Atlantic Ocean off the Hollywood oceanfront, Hallandale Beach city line north to John U. Lloyd Beach State Park (less any part in Dania Beach). Conservative reading: 100 yd measured from the seaward edge of the defined beach, i.e. 150 yd from MHW.
note: Read 7 Oct 2026 in Chrome on American Legal (rendered page text). NEW: not in the 30 Sep sweep, which could not reach Hollywood. Ambiguity: the lead-in limits § 99.03 to acts 'upon Hollywood Beach' (MHW to 50 yd) while (F) reaches 100 yd 'of' the beach; the conservative reading gives (F) its full reach measured from the beach's seaward edge. Whole Hollywood code not yet searched for other spear rules.

title: Pinellas County: no spearing in any manmade saltwater canal (hook and line, cast net and crab traps only)
effect: Taking or attempting to take any saltwater fish in any manmade saltwater canal in Pinellas County is unlawful except by hook and line, handheld cast net or up to five blue-crab traps, so spearfishing and gigging are excluded. Misdemeanor.
excerpt: (a) [Regulated.] It is unlawful for any person to take or attempt to take any saltwater fish, except by hook and line or handheld cast net or with no more than five blue-crab traps, within any manmade saltwater canal located in Pinellas County, Florida.
full: (b) [Penalty.] The violation of this section is declared to be a criminal offense and misdemeanor within the meaning of F.S. § 775.08, and shall be punishable as provided by law. (Ord. No. 25-28, § 1, 12-16-25). Sits in ch. 14, art. III, div. 2 'Saltwater Fishing', whose footnote says 'The acts contained in this division retain their status as special acts. See charter § 5.02.' and cites former F.S. § 370.172(4) and § 125.01(4).
scope: Every manmade saltwater canal in Pinellas County, on the face of the text including canals inside cities.
note: Read 7 Oct 2026 through api.municode.com in Chrome (client 7309, product 10274). NEW, adopted 16 Dec 2025. A gear-list rule that excludes spears by omission, like r. 68B-25.003. Open: whether it binds inside municipalities and whether it is a special act or a county ordinance; § 125.01(4) limits county power over saltwater fishing. Treated as live per project posture. Draw from canal polygons only if a public dataset carries manmade canals; otherwise a countywide text flag.

title: Town of Palm Beach: no fishing within 50 yards either side of guarded beaches; no swimming beyond 300 ft of them
effect: Fishing, which includes spearfishing, is unlawful in the waters 50 yards north or south of any lifeguarded Town beach, and swimming beyond 300 ft (from mean low water) of a lifeguarded Town beach is unlawful.
excerpt: (e) It shall be unlawful for any person to fish in the waters 50 yards in either direction north or south of any public beach operated and patrolled and guarded by lifeguards of the town.
full: § 74-162 history: (Ord. No. 8-96, § 1, 5-14-96; Ord. No. 21-10, § 1, 7-13-10; Ord. No. 003-2025, § 2, 3-4-25). § 74-197(a): 'It shall be declared unlawful for any person to swim beyond 300 feet of the shore of any public beach operated and patrolled and guarded by lifeguards of the town. For the purposes of this section, the 300-foot distance shall be measured at right angles from the mean low water mark of the Atlantic Ocean.' (b) applies to flotation aids. (Code 1982, § 14-61). § 74-269(a)(1) names the public beaches as 'Phipps Ocean Park, Mid Town Beach, Clarke Avenue Beach and Kreusler Park' for its 400 ft watercraft exclusion.
scope: Water off each lifeguarded Town of Palm Beach beach and 50 yd beyond each end (fishing); beyond 300 ft from MLW off those beaches (swimming).
note: Read 7 Oct 2026 through api.municode.com (client 9332, product 11397). NEW. Ch. 74 art. III is Boats and Boating; the sweep's 'art. III' lead meant the art. II beach rules. Reading of (e) that closes more water: the whole water off the guarded beach plus a 50-yard band each side. Guarded beaches are not listed in § 74-162; § 74-269 names four.

title: Deerfield Beach: no swimming beyond 50 yards of the beach without lifeguard permission; no fishing off the beach 8 a.m. to dusk
effect: Off the Deerfield Beach municipal beach, swimming more than 50 yards out from mean high water needs the supervising lifeguard's permission, and fishing off the beach (which includes shore-entry spearfishing) is unlawful from 8 a.m. to dusk.
excerpt: (b) Swim outside an area extending 50 yards eastward from the mean highwater mark of the Atlantic Ocean at the municipal/public beaches, unless express permission has been obtained from the supervising lifeguard.
full: Lead-in: 'It shall be unlawful for any person to do any acts set out in this section upon the municipal/public beaches of the city.' (p) 'Fish off of the municipal/public beaches, including the use of cast nets, from 8:00 a.m. to dusk.' § 50-2 extends the municipal/public beach to the wet sand seaward of mean high water.
scope: Atlantic Ocean off the Deerfield Beach municipal beach: beyond 50 yd from MHW (swimming, without permission); shore-based fishing from the beach 8 a.m. to dusk.
note: Read 7 Oct 2026 through api.municode.com. NEW. Conservative readings: a freediver or snorkeler is swimming; spearfishing is fishing; the lead-in's 'upon the municipal/public beaches' does not stop (b) applying in the water because (b) itself describes water. Warn, not closed: lifeguard permission can lift (b), and (p) is a daytime shore rule.
